recommendations.name: ‘AMA‘AMA – Contemporary Island Cooking
recommendations.reason: Mina's Fish House (5/5) and Roy's Ko Olina (food 5) show they want serious fish cookery with plated presentation right in Ko Olina; ‘AMA‘AMA is the same oceanfront, occasion-dinner register but with a fresher, brighter room than the one that cost Roy's its vibe score.
recommendations.avoids: Unlike Monkeypod Kitchen a few minutes away (quiet 1, music too loud), this is a low-volume, spaced-out dining room where conversation carries — their single biggest dealbreaker.
recommendations.dish: Whole or filleted local catch with island vegetables
recommendations.diet_fit: Kona kampachi, fresh daily island fish (opakapaka/monchong), poke starters and vegetable-forward sides — a full pescatarian main is standard here.

recommendations.name: Brick Oven Pizza
recommendations.reason: Moku Kitchen earned a 4 mainly on pizza; this is the neighborhood wood-fired version five minutes from home rather than a 24km drive.
recommendations.avoids: A small counter-service pizzeria rather than a bar-restaurant with a sound system, so it sidesteps the loud-music problem that dropped Monkeypod Kitchen to 3.
recommendations.diet_fit: Margherita and vegetable pizzas, plus cheese/marinara options — no meat required for a full meal.

recommendations.name: Thai Pho
recommendations.reason: Olay's Thai Lao is their 5/5 for curries and tom yum; this is the same flavor family without the 23km drive and paid parking they flagged at Olay's and Giovedi.
recommendations.avoids: A quiet strip-mall dining room, not a music-driven bar like Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Tofu or vegetable pad thai, green/red curry with tofu, and vegetarian pho — shrimp versions of most noodle dishes as well.

recommendations.name: Tropic Poke
recommendations.reason: They rate raw fish highest of anything — Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera 5/5, Katsumidori food 5 — and this is the casual, fresh-fish lunch version of that near Ko Olina.
recommendations.avoids: No dining-room stereo at all, so nothing like the noise that sank Restaurant 604 (quiet 1) applies.
recommendations.diet_fit: Ahi shoyu and spicy ahi poke bowls, salmon bowls — entirely fish-based.

recommendations.name: My Cafe
recommendations.reason: Their only local breakfast-leaning ratings are mid; this one is a mile from home and carries actual vegan cooking, useful for the pescatarian in the party who has to skip most Hawaii plate-lunch breakfasts.
recommendations.avoids: A small café, not a loud bar-restaurant like Monkeypod Kitchen, which they marked quiet 1.
recommendations.diet_fit: Vegan/vegetarian breakfast plates, avocado toast and bowls; ask about fish specials. Menu is documented as vegan-friendly.

recommendations.name: Taste of Hong Kong
recommendations.reason: Onkee Korean Grill House got a 5 for food-plus-value with no line; this is the same unglamorous, high-execution, good-value formula in a cuisine they haven't logged at all.
recommendations.avoids: A plain quiet dining room rather than the noise level that dropped Restaurant 604 to 3.
recommendations.diet_fit: Steamed whole fish, salt-and-pepper shrimp, ma po tofu (order vegetarian), and vegetable chow mein or greens with garlic.

recommendations.name: Kahumana - Organic Farm & Café
recommendations.reason: The Kini Room (5/5) and Mina's Fish House (5/5) show setting matters as much as the plate; Kahumana is the countryside equivalent — open-air tables looking at farm and mountains, food grown on site.
recommendations.avoids: About as far from Monkeypod Kitchen's amplified music (quiet 1) as Oahu offers; it is genuinely calm.
recommendations.dish: Farm salad with their own greens and the daily vegetarian curry
recommendations.diet_fit: Vegetarian lasagna, farm curry with brown rice, big garden salads and a rotating fish special — solid substantial pescatarian mains.

recommendations.name: Gyotaku
recommendations.reason: Katsumidori and Ginza Onodera prove they will drive for good Japanese fish; Gyotaku Pearl City does the sit-down izakaya version — sashimi and misoyaki butterfish — at a much saner price than Waikiki.
recommendations.avoids: Booth seating and a calm room, unlike Restaurant 604 where noise (quiet 1) outweighed the food.
recommendations.dish: Misoyaki butterfish
recommendations.diet_fit: Sashimi combinations, misoyaki butterfish, vegetable and shrimp tempura, chirashi bowls.

recommendations.name: Catania Ristorante Italiano
recommendations.reason: cino (4) and Giovedi (4) both scored well on food but lost points on a dark room and parking; a Pearl City trattoria gives them the same authentic Italian with easy free parking.
recommendations.avoids: Small-room Italian rather than the hard-surfaced noise box that made Restaurant 604 a 3.
recommendations.diet_fit: Seafood pastas (frutti di mare, vongole), eggplant parmigiana, margherita-style pizzas and risotto.

recommendations.name: Paesano
recommendations.reason: A long-running local Italian in the same lane as cino's 'authentic Italian food' note, and closer to home than Giovedi's Kakaako parking problem.
recommendations.avoids: Quiet suburban dining room, not the loud bar setting of Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Linguine with clams, shrimp scampi, eggplant parmigiana and meatless pasta primavera.

recommendations.name: The Elephant Shack
recommendations.reason: Olay's Thai Lao is a 5 for curries and tom yum; this one extends that toward the plant-based end, which matters for the pescatarian in the group who cannot take the usual chicken default.
recommendations.avoids: A tiny casual shop, so no amplified music like Monkeypod Kitchen's (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Vegan-tagged kitchen: tofu green curry, vegetable pad see ew, tom yum with tofu or shrimp.

recommendations.name: Patxi's Pizza
recommendations.reason: Moku Kitchen's 4 was carried by pizza; Patxi's deep dish is a different pizza idea entirely rather than a repeat of the same thin-crust pie.
recommendations.avoids: A sit-down room without the live-band volume that made Monkeypod Kitchen a 3.
recommendations.dish: Chicago-style deep dish, vegetarian
recommendations.diet_fit: Vegetarian deep dish (spinach/mushroom), margherita thin crust, salads — no meat needed.

recommendations.name: Aloha Poki
recommendations.reason: Given Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera's 5 for freshness, a dedicated poke counter is the weekday version of that same fish standard.
recommendations.avoids: Counter service, no dining-room music — nothing like the noise that sank Restaurant 604.
recommendations.diet_fit: Ahi, salmon and tako poke bowls — the whole menu is fish.

recommendations.name: Maharajas Foods (Vegan & Vegetarian)
recommendations.cuisine: lunch, dinner, indian, curry, rice, naan, asian, beans
recommendations.reason: Nothing in their library is Indian, and the household's pescatarian constraint is easiest to solve at an all-vegetarian kitchen; the spice-and-herb pull that makes Olay's Thai Lao a 5 translates directly.
recommendations.avoids: A small quiet vegetarian shop, the opposite of Monkeypod Kitchen's volume problem (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Entirely vegan/vegetarian: chana masala, dal, paneer-free curries, veg biryani and thali — everything is safe for the pescatarian.

recommendations.name: Clau & Chui's Cocina
recommendations.reason: They have no Mexican in their library at all, and their pattern — Onkee's 5 for unfussy food done well and priced well — suggests a small owner-run taqueria lands better than a themed chain.
recommendations.avoids: Order-at-the-counter quiet, not the loud bar room of Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Bean and cheese burritos, veggie tacos and quesadillas; shrimp or fish tacos if offered — I am not certain of the seafood lineup, so the vegetarian items are the reliable answer.

recommendations.name: Sasabune
recommendations.reason: Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera is their clearest 5 (food 5, service 5); Sasabune is the next rung up — chef-dictated omakase, warm rice, no menu — and it rewards exactly the freshness they praised.
recommendations.avoids: A hushed sushi counter where the room is deliberately quiet, the attribute that sank Restaurant 604 and Monkeypod Kitchen (both quiet 1).
recommendations.dish: The omakase, trusting the chef through the toro and the blue crab hand roll
recommendations.diet_fit: Omakase is entirely fish and shellfish, nigiri and hand rolls — perfect for a pescatarian.

recommendations.name: Sushi Sho
recommendations.reason: If Ginza Onodera at 5/5 is the bar, Sushi Sho is the once-a-year version of it — Edomae omakase at a tiny counter with the kind of service level they scored 5 across Olay's and Onkee.
recommendations.avoids: An intimate counter with no background noise whatsoever, unlike Restaurant 604 (quiet 1, food only 3).
recommendations.dish: The seasonal nigiri course, especially the kohada and the anago
recommendations.diet_fit: Fish-only omakase — nigiri, sashimi, tamago, pickled vegetables. Nothing for a pescatarian to navigate around.

recommendations.name: Yohei Sushi
recommendations.reason: Katsumidori got food 5 but vibe 2 for a dated interior; Yohei is the same traditional-sushi quality in a calm, well-kept Kalihi room, so the food score holds and the vibe score stops dragging.
recommendations.avoids: Directly answers the Katsumidori problem — a tidy, quiet counter instead of an outdated, noisy space like Restaurant 604.
recommendations.dish: Nigiri sampler with local fish
recommendations.diet_fit: Nigiri, sashimi, chirashi and vegetable rolls; miso soup and chawanmushi as sides.

recommendations.name: MW Restaurant
recommendations.reason: Mina's Fish House (5/5, presentation praised) and Roy's Ko Olina (food 5, dessert great) point straight at MW — modern Hawaii cooking with serious plating and a famously good dessert program — but in a bright contemporary room rather than Roy's dated one.
recommendations.avoids: Fixes the exact flaw of Roy's Ko Olina (vibe 2, outdated interior) without giving up the food level.
recommendations.dish: Mochi-crusted fresh catch, then the candy-bar dessert
recommendations.diet_fit: Mochi-crusted opakapaka or daily island fish, poke starters and vegetable sides — a full pescatarian dinner is easy here.

recommendations.name: Miro Kaimuki
recommendations.reason: Rigo Spanish Italian got a 5 for food and vibe together; Miro is the same idea — a small chef-driven room where the cooking and the setting are one piece — in a French-Japanese idiom they have never tried.
recommendations.avoids: A small, low-volume dining room, the opposite of Restaurant 604's noise (quiet 1) that outweighed decent food.
recommendations.dish: The tasting menu with the seafood courses
recommendations.diet_fit: Tasting menu leans heavily on fish and vegetables; they will generally build a pescatarian path — worth phoning ahead to confirm, which is why I'm not fully certain.

recommendations.name: Mud Hen Water
recommendations.reason: Between Mina's Fish House (5) and Moku Kitchen (4), they like Hawaii ingredients handled with intent; Mud Hen Water is the small-plates, share-the-table version with a lanai like the terrace they loved at The Kini Room.
recommendations.avoids: Neighborhood-scale and conversational rather than the amplified Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1).
recommendations.dish: Poi and lomi-style shared plates with the fish of the day
recommendations.diet_fit: Poke, grilled fish, limu and vegetable small plates, ulu and taro dishes — genuinely strong non-meat menu.

recommendations.name: Mimi's Peruvian Cuisine
recommendations.reason: Rigo Spanish Italian (5/5) shows they respond to Spanish-inflected cooking, and their raw-fish love at Ginza Onodera makes ceviche the obvious unexplored bridge — citrus-cured fish rather than another sushi bar.
recommendations.avoids: A modest family dining room, not the loud bar format that dropped Monkeypod Kitchen to 3.
recommendations.dish: Ceviche mixto
recommendations.diet_fit: Ceviche, jalea (fried seafood), arroz con mariscos and chaufa de mariscos — the seafood side of a Peruvian menu is large.

recommendations.name: Middle Eats
recommendations.reason: A cuisine entirely absent from their library, and one that solves the pescatarian problem structurally; the herb-and-spice intensity they praise at Olay's Thai Lao carries over to za'atar, sumac and tahini.
recommendations.avoids: Small casual counter — none of the music-volume issue that marked Monkeypod Kitchen quiet 1.
recommendations.diet_fit: Falafel plates, hummus and mujadara, grilled vegetable mezze; often a grilled fish or shrimp plate as well.

recommendations.name: Tadka Indian Cuisine
recommendations.reason: They have no Indian at all and they clearly like layered, aromatic food (Olay's curries, 5/5); a proper North Indian kitchen with a big vegetarian half is the natural extension.
recommendations.avoids: Calm restaurant service, unlike Restaurant 604 where the noise (quiet 1) ruined an otherwise okay meal.
recommendations.diet_fit: Paneer tikka masala, dal makhani, chana masala, baingan bharta, veg biryani, plus fish or shrimp curry on most Indian menus.

recommendations.name: Water Drop Vegetarian House
recommendations.reason: An entirely meat-free Chinese kitchen removes all friction for the pescatarian in the party — something none of their current favorites (Onkee, Katsumidori) do — while keeping the Asian flavors they eat most happily.
recommendations.avoids: A quiet, plain Chinatown dining room, nothing like Monkeypod Kitchen's music level (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Entirely vegetarian: braised tofu claypots, mock-meat noodle dishes, vegetable dumplings, hot and sour soup — every item is safe.

recommendations.name: Legend Seafood Restaurant
recommendations.reason: Their highest scores cluster on fish handled well (Mina's Fish House, Ginza Onodera); Legend is the Cantonese answer — live tanks, steamed whole fish, cart dim sum — a format they have never logged.
recommendations.avoids: Honest caveat: a dim sum hall at peak hours is loud, which is their dealbreaker (Restaurant 604, quiet 1) — go at 2pm on a weekday or at dinner for the seafood menu, when the room is calm.
recommendations.dish: Steamed whole fish with ginger and scallion
recommendations.diet_fit: Steamed fish, shrimp har gow, scallop and vegetable dumplings, garlic greens, tofu claypot — the seafood and vegetable half of the menu is enormous.

recommendations.name: Lobster King
recommendations.reason: Mina's Fish House got a 5 for fish plus occasion; Lobster King is the unglamorous, high-value version of a seafood feast, which matches the value-5 satisfaction they recorded at Onkee.
recommendations.avoids: Not a bar-with-band setup like Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1); it's a plain restaurant focused on the table.
recommendations.diet_fit: Lobster in ginger and scallion, steamed fish, salt-and-pepper shrimp, crab with garlic noodles, tofu and vegetable dishes.

recommendations.name: Pizza Mamo
recommendations.reason: Moku Kitchen scored a 4 largely on pizza; Pizza Mamo is the serious, blistered-crust Chinatown version and a clear upgrade rather than a repeat.
recommendations.avoids: A tiny slice-and-table shop, not the live-music bar volume that capped Monkeypod Kitchen at 3.
recommendations.dish: The Mamo pie by the slice
recommendations.diet_fit: Cheese and vegetable pies (mushroom, onion) — a full meal without meat toppings.

recommendations.name: O’Kims
recommendations.reason: Onkee Korean Grill House is a 5 across food, service and value; O'Kims is the non-grill Korean counterpart — banchan, stews, outdoor seating — so the party's pescatarian isn't stuck watching a meat grill.
recommendations.avoids: Patio and small dining room rather than the amplified interior of Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1).
recommendations.dish: Haemul pajeon (seafood pancake)
recommendations.diet_fit: Seafood pancake, sundubu jjigae with tofu/seafood, bibimbap without meat, and documented vegan options.

recommendations.name: Keo's Kitchen
recommendations.reason: Olay's Thai Lao earned a 5 for curries and tom yum; Keo's carries a vegetarian-friendly kitchen so the same dishes work for the whole table without the chicken default.
recommendations.avoids: Sit-down room with normal conversation levels — not the music problem of Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Tofu green and red curry, Evil Jungle Prince with tofu or shrimp, tom yum goong, vegetable pad thai.

recommendations.name: Thai Vientiane Restaurant
recommendations.reason: Olay's Thai Lao is their only 5-star Lao food and the notes read like the draw is the Lao side — the herbs and the sour-chili edge. This is the other Thai-Lao kitchen on the island, so it extends the actual preference rather than adding a fifth generic Thai.
recommendations.avoids: Small family-run dining room, none of the volume that made Monkeypod Kitchen a 3.
recommendations.diet_fit: Green papaya salad, tofu larb, vegetable and tofu curries, tom yum with shrimp, sticky rice — the Lao repertoire is easy to keep meat-free.

recommendations.name: SingSing Thai Street Food
recommendations.reason: A punchier, street-stall take on the flavors Olay's Thai Lao earned a 5 for, useful when they want the chili and herbs without the full sit-down dinner.
recommendations.avoids: Counter-scale and low-key, unlike Restaurant 604 where noise (quiet 1) overrode merely okay food.
recommendations.diet_fit: Tofu boat noodles, papaya salad, vegetable stir-fries and shrimp dishes.

recommendations.name: Bernini
recommendations.reason: cino (food 4) was marked down for a dark interior and Giovedi for parking; Bernini gives them the same careful Italian cooking in a brighter, calmer room, and it's the sort of place Rigo's 5 suggests they'd enjoy.
recommendations.avoids: Quiet, low-lit-but-not-gloomy dining room — steers clear of both cino's dark interior and Restaurant 604's noise (quiet 1).
recommendations.dish: Seafood risotto
recommendations.diet_fit: Seafood pasta and risotto, caprese, eggplant and vegetarian primi — a real pescatarian main, not a side.

recommendations.name: Fresh Catch
recommendations.reason: Mina's Fish House at 5/5 shows fish is the throughline; Fresh Catch is the everyday version — poke by the pound and grilled fish plates — with the kind of value that earned Onkee its 5.
recommendations.avoids: Order-at-the-counter format with no soundtrack, so nothing like Restaurant 604's noise (quiet 1).
recommendations.dish: Garlic ahi poke bowl
recommendations.diet_fit: Poke bowls (ahi, tako, salmon), grilled or misoyaki fish plates, seared ahi — the menu is fish-first.

recommendations.name: Kayak Cafe
recommendations.reason: Their breakfast slot is unfilled and Eggs 'n Things-style tourist rooms would repeat the Monkeypod noise problem; Kayak is small, vegetarian-friendly and calm.
recommendations.avoids: A quiet neighborhood café, explicitly unlike Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1, music too loud).
recommendations.diet_fit: Vegetarian breakfast plates, avocado toast, veggie scrambles and bowls; smoked-salmon options are common.

recommendations.name: Shaloha
recommendations.reason: No Mediterranean anywhere in their library, and their Rigo (Spanish-Italian, 5/5) score shows the Mediterranean palate lands; this is the casual, garlicky end of it.
recommendations.avoids: Tiny quiet shop, not the loud bar format of Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Falafel pita and plate, greek salad with feta, hummus platters; often a fish souvlaki option.

recommendations.name: Nico’s Pier 38
recommendations.reason: They gave food 5 to Roy's and Mina's for fish; Nico's buys straight off the auction floor next door, delivering the same freshness at Onkee-level value (value 5 was a real factor for them).
recommendations.avoids: Honest note: the dining hall is busy at lunch, which touches their quiet dealbreaker (Restaurant 604, quiet 1) — the outdoor harbor tables or an off-peak visit fix it, and the fish quality is worth the timing.
recommendations.dish: Furikake pan-seared ahi
recommendations.diet_fit: Furikake ahi, fish and chips, poke bowls, grilled catch of the day — the whole identity is fish.

recommendations.name: Pho Saigon
recommendations.reason: Vietnamese is missing from their list despite how much Southeast Asian food they rate highly (Olay's, 5/5); the herb plate and broth aromatics are the same pleasure, and this kitchen keeps genuinely meat-free versions.
recommendations.avoids: Simple quiet noodle house, nothing like Monkeypod Kitchen's volume (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Vegetarian pho with tofu and vegetable broth, tofu vermicelli bowls, fresh spring rolls — vegan options are documented here rather than assumed.

recommendations.name: Maguro Spot
recommendations.reason: Direct extension of the Ginza Onodera 5 — very fresh tuna, minimal fuss, fast — for the days they don't want a 28km sushi-counter commitment.
recommendations.avoids: Counter service, no music issue of the kind that sank Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Maguro and salmon poke bowls, negitoro, sashimi plates; vegan-tagged sides too.

recommendations.name: Arancino di Mare
recommendations.reason: cino and Giovedi both got 4s for authentic Italian; Arancino di Mare is the seafood-Italian version, which also ties in Mina's Fish House (5/5) — pasta with island fish rather than another red-sauce room.
recommendations.avoids: A composed, softly-lit dining room — avoids both cino's too-dark interior and Restaurant 604's noise (quiet 1).
recommendations.dish: Sea urchin cream spaghetti
recommendations.diet_fit: Uni pasta, frutti di mare linguine, clam spaghetti, caprese and vegetable antipasti — pescatarian is the house strength.

recommendations.name: Taormina
recommendations.reason: Rigo's 5 for food and atmosphere together is the template, and Taormina does Sicilian seafood pasta in a calm Waikiki room with attentive service (they average service 5, so this matters).
recommendations.avoids: Quiet, unhurried dining room, unlike Restaurant 604 (quiet 1) where noise wrecked the meal.
recommendations.dish: Spaghetti alle vongole
recommendations.diet_fit: Vongole, seafood risotto, swordfish and grilled fish mains, eggplant caponata.

recommendations.name: Hau Tree Lanai
recommendations.reason: The Kini Room (vibe 5, terrace) and Mina's Fish House (view, terrace) are their two clearest 5s for setting; Hau Tree is dining under the tree right on Kaimana Beach, which is the best version of that idea on the island.
recommendations.avoids: Open-air and ocean-quiet rather than the indoor amplified music that dropped Monkeypod Kitchen to 3.
recommendations.dish: Eggs Benedict with smoked salmon at brunch, or the grilled catch at dinner
recommendations.diet_fit: Grilled fresh catch, poke, smoked-salmon benedict, seafood salads — reliable pescatarian mains.

recommendations.name: Deck
recommendations.reason: The Kini Room got 5s for mocktails, terrace seating and happy hour; Deck is the same formula with a Diamond Head view — and they've shown mocktail programs are part of how they judge a place (Giovedi, Rigo).
recommendations.avoids: Open rooftop air disperses sound, avoiding the boxed-in loudness that made Restaurant 604 a 3.
recommendations.dish: Ahi poke with the sunset happy hour
recommendations.diet_fit: Ahi poke, fish tacos, grilled catch, vegetable flatbreads — a full pescatarian meal off the regular menu.

recommendations.name: Búho Cocina y Cantina
recommendations.reason: Rooftop terrace, house mocktails and a view — exactly what earned The Kini Room a 5 — but in Mexican, a cuisine entirely missing from their thirteen rated places.
recommendations.avoids: Open-air rooftop rather than an enclosed loud bar like Monkeypod Kitchen (quiet 1); go early evening for the calmest table.
recommendations.dish: Fish tacos with the guacamole made tableside
recommendations.diet_fit: Fish and shrimp tacos, ceviche, veggie enchiladas and mushroom quesadillas.

recommendations.name: Morimoto Asia Waikiki
recommendations.reason: Bridges two of their 5s — the sushi standard of Ginza Onodera and the presentation-and-occasion pull of Mina's Fish House — with a bright modern room that fixes the vibe-2 complaint they logged at Katsumidori and Roy's.
recommendations.avoids: Spacious, well-designed dining room rather than the outdated interior that cost Roy's Ko Olina and Katsumidori their vibe scores.
recommendations.dish: Black cod miso
recommendations.diet_fit: Black cod miso, sushi and sashimi, tuna pizza, seafood ramen variants and vegetable dishes.

recommendations.name: TsuruTonTan
recommendations.reason: They love Japanese but only via sushi (Onodera 5, Katsumidori food 5); hand-cut udon in giant bowls is the same culture, a different pleasure, and the room is far nicer than Katsumidori's dated one.
recommendations.avoids: Modern, comfortable interior — the direct fix for Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo's vibe 2 'outdated interior' note.
recommendations.dish: Mentaiko cream udon
recommendations.diet_fit: Mentaiko cream udon, tempura shrimp udon, kake udon with kombu-dashi, vegetable tempura — all fish/veg based.

recommendations.name: Noi Thai Cuisine
recommendations.reason: Olay's Thai Lao is a 5 but the notes flag paid parking and a plain setting; Noi is the polished-room version of the same curries and tom yum, which fits their pattern of rewarding vibe alongside food (Rigo, 5/5).
recommendations.avoids: A quiet, formally set dining room, unlike Monkeypod Kitchen's music (quiet 1).
recommendations.dish: Tom yum goong
recommendations.diet_fit: Tom yum goong, tofu or shrimp green curry, vegetable pad thai, papaya salad.

recommendations.name: Udon Yama
recommendations.reason: A small specialist noodle counter — the same single-focus craft that made Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera a 5 — in a category they've never rated.
recommendations.avoids: Tiny quiet shop, the opposite of Restaurant 604's noise problem (quiet 1).
recommendations.diet_fit: Kake and bukkake udon in kombu/bonito dashi, shrimp and vegetable tempura udon — meat-free bowls are standard.

recommendations.name: Haleʻiwa Beach House
recommendations.reason: Mina's Fish House (5/5, view and terrace) and The Kini Room (5/5, terrace and mocktails) define their best nights out; this is the North Shore equivalent and gives them a whole different side of the island to make a day of.
recommendations.avoids: Open-air plantation-style room with sea air rather than the boxed-in loudness that sank Restaurant 604 (quiet 1).
recommendations.dish: Grilled catch with the beachside table
recommendations.diet_fit: Fresh catch of the day, poke, fish tacos, seafood pasta and vegetable sides.

recommendations.name: Banzai Sushi Bar
recommendations.reason: Pairs the sushi standard they set at Ginza Onodera (5/5) with the garden-terrace setting that made The Kini Room a 5 — low tables, outdoor seating, live acoustic sets rather than a stereo.
recommendations.avoids: Outdoor garden seating means live, acoustic sound rather than the blaring recorded music that dropped Monkeypod Kitchen to 3.
recommendations.dish: Sashimi plate with the fresh local catch
recommendations.diet_fit: Sashimi and nigiri, vegetable and seafood rolls, edamame, seaweed salad, miso soup.
